bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

sections.Key Messages:
- Mild and dry conditions on tap today and Wednesday.
- Patchy fog is possible in the lower valleys Wednesday morning
  as a result of clearing skies and high relative humidities.
- Active weather remains possible late this week, but some
  details remain uncertain at this time. Stay tuned for updates
  to timing and impacts as they become available.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 957 AM MST Tue Nov 24 2026
MILD AND DRY CONDITIONS TODAY AND WEDNESDAY:
A fast moving ridge will begin to build into the area today in the
wake of the previous system. This will cause generally mild and dry
conditions for much of the region through Wednesday. Additionally,
daytime highs for today and Wednesday will be hovering around normal
for much of the region. Patchy fog could be a possibility again
Wednesday morning in the lower valleys as overnight clearing
skies in combination with high relative humidities will favor
fog formation. There is a particularly strong signal for high
relative humidities in the Uinta Basin area, but cloud cover
will heavily dictate the fog that forms in that location.
ANOTHER SYSTEM EXPECTED AFTER THANKSGIVING:
As the current ridge shifts eastward, deterministic guidance
indicates a split flow pattern developing by Thursday. A new
ridge will build over Southern California, leaving our region
sandwiched between a cutoff low to the south and stronger
systems to our north and east. This setup will maintain
generally dry conditions and above-normal temperatures through
Thanksgiving. By Friday, the Southern California ridge will
break down as the next system approaches. Resulting
northwesterly flow will favor snowfall over the Park Range
Friday and Saturday. Because model projections for snow totals
continue to fluctuate daily, confidence in exact amounts remains
low. However, anyone traveling late this week should prepare
for potentially difficult conditions, especially across the
northern mountains. Light impacts are also possible south of the
Park Range, though confidence there is low as well. Please
continue to monitor the forecast, as details will likely evolve
over the coming days. Looking ahead to Sunday and early next
week, models diverge on specific scenarios, though the overall
pattern appears likely to remain unsettled.
sections.Aviation:
Issued at 408 PM MST Tue Nov 24 2026
Aside from some passing high clouds, skies will remain mostly
clear through the next 24 hours. Fog and low stratus are
expected to redevelop around KDRO, with VCFG in the TAF between
06z and 12z. Winds will be light and terrain driven through the
period. VFR conditions will prevail, though drops to MVFR/IFR
will be possible at KDRO in fog or low stratus due to reduced
ceilings and/or visibility.
